packageLicense: MIT, verified from the pinned wheel license file
findings: Pydoll and Rebrowser each matched 5/16 selected observations, with no exclusive matches: GitHub/arXiv in both rounds plus Lowes only in round one.
The four-cell Rebrowser comparison matched Lowes 0/4 in every proxy-scope/interception cell; each GitHub control passed.
On the unchanged production service, consent off and rejectNonEssential each matched 2/12, all GitHub controls. Neither retrieved the five selected persistent failures.
Lowes first-round frozen HTML marker matches did not contain the complete expected sentence in captured rendered body text; the displayed heading was shorter. The frozen grader was not changed.
Two Pydoll G2 observations failed stable capture after a 403 navigation; they remain adapter errors, not proof of a different WAF rule.

Pydoll compatibility accepts service_workers but its inspected context implementation does not enforce blocking. The driver comparison deliberately allowed service workers in both experimental profiles; it is not a production replacement.
limits: Selected live observations are not a full-target or WAF-vendor rate, a controlled code-version gain, extraction F1 or hosted parity.
The driver comparison includes launcher and protocol differences, captured in process arguments; it does not isolate a single CDP method.
Production consent/readiness/session behavior was not ported into the driver prototype. Only the separate consent experiment used the unchanged production browser service.
Normalized HTML marker retrieval and rendered exact-marker presence are separate measures. No expected text was sent to the browser workers.
decision: Keep the existing production driver, guarded routing and consent defaults. These experiments did not establish a repeatable coverage gain.
